chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyād, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled regarding a slave who stole and misappropriated from the wealth of his master, saying: “There is no amputation upon him.”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام as the Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.اخْتَانَ: acted dishonestly by misappropriating property entrusted or accessible to him
key_terms.قَضَى: issued a legal judgment or ruling
key_terms.قَطْعٌ: the legal amputation penalty prescribed for theft in certain cases
key_terms.مَالِ مَوْلَاهُ: the wealth or property of his master

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a slave steals from the wealth of his master?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning a slave who took from the property of his master. The ruling states that the prescribed amputation penalty for theft does not apply in this case, indicating a specific legal exception in the law of theft.
